description_full: Cadeler plc, together with its subsidiaries, operates as an offshore wind installation vessel contractor in Denmark, the United Kingdom, Germany, Poland, rest of Europe, the United States, and Taiwan. The company engages in the transport and installation of offshore wind turbine generators, foundations, and topsides and substations; maintenance of offshore wind turbine generators, and offshore structures and platforms; and offshore construction within renewable space. It also involved offshore decommissioning within renewable space; salvage assistance; and heavy lift and project cargo. In addition, the company owns and operates ten offshore jack-up windfarm installation vessels. Further, it also provides hydraulic pile driving solutions. Cadeler plc was incorporated in 2008 and is based in Norwich, United Kingdom.

financial_summary: Cadeler A/S is a mid-cap industrials business with a $2.6B market cap on $691M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +144% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 5% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 50% confirm genuine pricing power.
The company is burning through $938M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 4.2× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and interest coverage runs at 8.5×.
Shareholder yield is only 0.1%, a thin return of capital, and within its sector the business captures 4.7× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
